Comorbidity indicators

Source: vignettes/articles/comorbidity.Rmd
comorbidity.Rmd

nis_comorbidity() uses the optional medicalcoder package to apply its AHRQ Elixhauser ICD-10-CM mapping. easyNIS does not distribute clinical code lists. This computation is experimental and its assumptions need scientific review.

Score a DuckDB cohort

Keep KEY_NIS and, for pooled years, YEAR with the diagnosis columns. The function scores batches of up to 25,000 discharges, reading only the keys, diagnoses and available POA fields into the scoring workflow. The result remains a DuckDB query with the original columns and the added indicators. Select the columns you need before collecting.

The example assigns stable keys to the invented fixture. NIS files already include KEY_NIS.

discharges <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  dplyr::filter(AGE >= 18) |>
  dplyr::mutate(KEY_NIS = dplyr::row_number()) |>
  dplyr::compute()
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3dKXJP/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3dKXJP/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
scored <- nis_comorbidity(discharges)
#> Warning: No matching POA column for 40 diagnosis slots: I10_DX1, I10_DX10, I10_DX11,
#> I10_DX12, I10_DX13, I10_DX14, I10_DX15, I10_DX16, I10_DX17, I10_DX18, I10_DX19,
#> I10_DX2, I10_DX20, I10_DX21, I10_DX22, I10_DX23, I10_DX24, I10_DX25, I10_DX26,
#> I10_DX27, I10_DX28, I10_DX29, I10_DX3, I10_DX30, I10_DX31, I10_DX32, I10_DX33,
#> I10_DX34, I10_DX35, I10_DX36, I10_DX37, I10_DX38, I10_DX39, I10_DX4, I10_DX40,
#> I10_DX5, I10_DX6, I10_DX7, I10_DX8, I10_DX9. Assuming present.
#> ℹ POA-dependent comorbidities may include conditions acquired in hospital.
scored |>
  dplyr::select(AGE, cmrb_n, cmrb_any, cmrb_mortality_index) |>
  head() |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>     AGE cmrb_n cmrb_any cmrb_mortality_index
#>   <dbl>  <int> <lgl>                   <int>
#> 1    28      1 TRUE                       14
#> 2    35      1 TRUE                        0
#> 3    42      1 TRUE                        0
#> 4    49      0 FALSE                       0
#> 5    56      1 TRUE                       14
#> 6    63      1 TRUE                        0

The added columns report the number of flagged conditions and whether any were flagged. Values are computed from invented codes. Rows without usable ICD-10 codes have missing results rather than “no comorbidity.”

Scores are computed when you call nis_comorbidity() and kept in a temporary table for the input connection. DuckDB reads the original query again when you use its output, so score a stable cohort with unique, non-missing keys. Collected data frames are also supported and keep their original row order.

Add scores after design construction

If an analysis uses nis_design(), keep diagnosis columns in the design and pass the design to nis_comorbidity(). This preserves the design object.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3dKXJP/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3dKXJP/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure,
  keep = c(AGE, dplyr::starts_with("I10_DX"), dplyr::starts_with("DXPOA"))
)
#> Cohort: 54 discharges; weighted N 62.4; 9 hospitals across 1 years.
scored_design <- nis_comorbidity(design)
#> Warning: No matching POA column for 40 diagnosis slots: I10_DX1, I10_DX10, I10_DX11,
#> I10_DX12, I10_DX13, I10_DX14, I10_DX15, I10_DX16, I10_DX17, I10_DX18, I10_DX19,
#> I10_DX2, I10_DX20, I10_DX21, I10_DX22, I10_DX23, I10_DX24, I10_DX25, I10_DX26,
#> I10_DX27, I10_DX28, I10_DX29, I10_DX3, I10_DX30, I10_DX31, I10_DX32, I10_DX33,
#> I10_DX34, I10_DX35, I10_DX36, I10_DX37, I10_DX38, I10_DX39, I10_DX4, I10_DX40,
#> I10_DX5, I10_DX6, I10_DX7, I10_DX8, I10_DX9. Assuming present.
#> ℹ POA-dependent comorbidities may include conditions acquired in hospital.
head(scored_design$variables[c("AGE", "cmrb_n", "cmrb_any")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>     AGE cmrb_n cmrb_any
#>   <dbl>  <int> <lgl>   
#> 1    28      1 TRUE    
#> 2    35      1 TRUE    
#> 3    49      0 FALSE   
#> 4    56      1 TRUE    
#> 5    70      1 TRUE    
#> 6    77      1 TRUE

The survey design fields remain the same while the analysis variables gain comorbidity indicators.

Present on admission

AHRQ assigns 18 of its 38 refined Elixhauser measures using POA for nonexempt secondary diagnoses. For those diagnoses, Y and W qualify. NIS files lack POA indicators. AHRQ leaves those 18 measures missing when POA inputs are unavailable and requires all 38 to calculate its indices. Beginning in 2019, the NIS Diagnosis and Procedure Groups file includes the available HCUP-derived measures. AHRQ User Guide, HCUP POA availability, 2019 NIS introduction.

nis_comorbidity() retains its experimental assumption that a diagnosis was present on admission when its entire DXPOAn field is absent. The warning identifies the affected slots. This assumption can count conditions that arose during the stay and alter the mortality and readmission scores. When a matching field is present, Y and W count as POA, N and U do not, and other values are unknown. In pooled data, a missing value in an existing POA column remains unknown. medicalcoder supplies the exempt-code mapping, which is shared across AHRQ releases in that package and is applied without looking up the fiscal year for each discharge.

Pre-October 2015 ICD-9 records receive missing results. Older Stata-derived ynel* and elixsum fields use different definitions and versions.

Charlson in NIS studies

Charlson serves different purposes across studies. The national inpatient norms study used Quan’s ICD-10 algorithms to describe comorbidity burden by demographic groups. The NIS hepatitis C pregnancy study used the Charlson–Deyo score as an adjustment covariate, grouping it into 0, 1–2, and above 2. National norms study, hepatitis C pregnancy study.

easyNIS defers a Charlson option until it can specify and verify the mapping, weights, diagnosis inclusion, and POA assumptions for a named variant. medicalcoder supplies Quan 2005 and 2011 variants, with distinct weights and explicit POA and principal-diagnosis inputs. The comorbidity package offers a Quan ICD-10 map with separately selectable original or revised weights and a severity hierarchy. For a replication, choose these inputs using the study’s methods. medicalcoder Charlson vignette, comorbidity manual.

See nis_comorbidity() and Data notes by year.
